# IS 360 · Midterm Study Plan

**Exam:** 2026-11-05 (Thu) 10:00 — Room B-12
**Strategy:** one focused session per day (~60–90 min), one topic per day, light day before the exam.
Short daily blocks > all-nighters (see Lessons in MEMORY.MD).

| # | Date | Focus | Done ✅ |
|---|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Fri 2026-10-30 | Security fundamentals: CIA triad, threats vs. vulnerabilities vs. risks, security controls | ☐ |
| 2 | Sat 2026-10-31 | Authentication & access control: MFA, AAA, DAC/MAC/RBAC, password policies | ☐ |
| 3 | Sun 2026-11-01 | Cryptography — part 1: symmetric (AES), key distribution problem → notes/security/week-6-crypto.md | ☐ |
| 4 | Mon 2026-11-02 | Cryptography — part 2: asymmetric (RSA), digital signatures, hashing & salting (SHA-256), PKI/certificates | ☐ |
| 5 | Tue 2026-11-03 | Network & data security: firewalls, VPN/TLS, common attacks (MITM, phishing, DoS, injection) + defenses | ☐ |
| 6 | Wed 2026-11-04 | Full review: past papers / self-quiz, re-read weak spots, skim all notes. Finish by 22:00, sleep early. | ☐ |

**Exam day:** Thu 2026-11-05, arrive at B-12 by 09:40.

## Notes
- Day 5 is the heaviest day — it links crypto (days 3–4) to real-world defenses, expect it to run long.
- If a session slips, don't skip ahead: compress the missed topic into the review day.

<file path="notes/security/week-6-crypto.md" lines="1-5 of 5">
# Information Security · Week 6: cryptography basics

- Symmetric encryption (AES): one shared key; fast; key distribution is the hard part.
- Asymmetric encryption (RSA): public/private key pair; slower; used for key exchange and signatures.
- Hash functions (SHA-256): one-way, fixed-length digest; used for integrity and password storage (with a salt).
</file>
